name: xero-overdue-invoice-to-gmail-reminder

trigger.authentication_note: Xero work.flowers. The same credential is ALSO bound as the `xero_wf` connection alias, because the workflow body re-reads the invoice.
trigger.trigger_note: Polling trigger (Overdue Sales Invoice), one run per invoice. `days_overdue` is sent as the NUMBER 1, not the string "1" the classic Zap carried: `list-trigger-input-fields` gives it `type: number`, and a scalar/array or string/number mismatch in trigger params makes the trigger claim fail SILENTLY at publish — the publish returns success and the workflow just stays disabled. Confirmed claimed here (`status: active`). The classic Zap also carried polling_interval_override: 15, which the durable --trigger payload has no field for; the default interval applies.

connections_note: gmail_wf is the shared `dennis@work.flowers` connection (GoogleMailV2CLIAPI@2.14.0), matching the classic Zap's Gmail step version. The other Gmail connection in the account, `Gmail dennis@work.flowers` (02a57b11-…), is pinned to GoogleMailV2CLIAPI@1.1.12 and is the one gmail-attachments-to-drive-by-type uses on its trigger — do not swap them.
version_pinning_note: Matches every other Durable in this repo. All three are the newest versions published at least 24h before build time, which is what the Vercel sandbox's `pnpm install --config.minimumReleaseAge=1440` requires.

tasks_per_run.note: Same as the classic Zap, which also spent a lookup plus a Gmail step.

email.why_draft: Preserved from the classic Zap. A debt-chasing email goes out only after a person has read it. Nothing in this workflow can send.
email.from: Not set. The Gmail connection is dennis@work.flowers, so the default sender is already right, and `from` is a dynamic enum that rejects an unvalidated literal.
email.to: Contact.EmailAddress. If the contact has none but its contact persons do, they are promoted to To rather than drafting a Cc-only email.
email.cc: Every Contact.ContactPersons[].EmailAddress with IncludeInEmails !== false, minus anyone already in To.
email.attachment: The invoice PDF, from find_invoice_by_id with include_pdf: true (an opaque Zapier `hydrate|||…|||hydrate` file ref passed straight to Gmail's `file` input).

verified_cases.result: outcome 'reminder-drafted', draft 19fa8c76377a87ba. Confirmed present in Gmail with the composed body, to ap.scw@securecodewarrior.com, cc jaap@scw.io. Deleted afterwards (it was a test against an invoice that is not actually overdue) — verified gone from Drafts.

dry_run_note: A manual run accepts `{"InvoiceID": "<guid or INV-nnnn>", "dryRun": true}` and returns the composed reminder without creating a draft. The Xero trigger never sets `dryRun`.
description: Xero sales invoice 1 day overdue -> re-read the invoice for its online-invoice URL and PDF and, only if it is still awaiting payment, create a Gmail DRAFT reminder to the customer with the invoice PDF attached. Never sends. Migration of the classic Zap 'Overdue Invoice Reminders (1 Day)'. Fixes the PDF attachment (which pointed at a non-existent trigger field), the body line that told customers their invoice came from themselves, and adds a still-owed guard.

version_history.note: Initial migration, published disabled for testing. Superseded: its toIsoDate used `new Date(ms)`, which the durable runtime rejects.

Replaced `new Date(ms)` with integer civil-from-days arithmetic and enabled. The sibling Zap hit `DeterminismViolation: Non-deterministic API "new Date()" called in GUARDED mode` on that code path; this workflow had the same latent fault, reached whenever a date arrives as `/Date(ms)/` with no `…String` variant. The replacement was checked against native Date across a 50,000-day sweep plus 2000-02-29 and 2100-02-28.

replaces_classic_zap.title: Overdue Invoice Reminders (1 Day)
replaces_classic_zap.old_shape: XeroCLIAPI@2.20.5 overdue_sales_invoice (days_overdue: "1") -> XeroCLIAPI find_invoice_by_id (include_pdf: false, include_online_url: true) -> GoogleMailV2CLIAPI@2.14.0 write `draft_v2`.
replaces_classic_zap.status: The trigger was live (`paused: false`) but BOTH action steps were `paused: true`, so the Zap polled Xero and then did nothing. Turn it off rather than unpausing, or it and this workflow will both draft the same reminder.
known_issues_fixed: The draft's attachment was mapped to `gives[trigger].InvoicePDF` — the TRIGGER's output, not the lookup's — while the lookup was configured with `include_pdf: false`. So no PDF was fetched and the field referenced did not exist: the reminder never carried the invoice. Now `include_pdf: true` and the returned file ref is attached (verified: draft 19fa8c76377a87ba).
The body read 'the following invoice from {{Contact.Name}} is now overdue', interpolating the CUSTOMER's own name — so it told them their invoice came from themselves. Now reads 'from workFlowers'.

No check that the invoice was still owed. The trigger polls a due-date window, so an invoice paid, voided or credited between the poll and the run would still have been chased. Verified against INV-0075, which the durable declines.
`Cc` was every contact person including one whose address is the contact's own, so a customer could be both To'd and Cc'd. Now deduped case-insensitively.
Xero's IncludeInEmails flag on a contact person was ignored.
A contact with no email address at all produced a draft addressed to nobody. Now skipped with a reason.
`DueDateString` was pasted raw into the body, rendering as `2026-08-02T00:00:00`. Now `2026-08-02`.
`AmountDue` was pasted raw, so a float could render as `7398.170000000001`. Now two decimal places, thousands-separated.
`days_overdue` was the string "1" against a number-typed field (see trigger_note).
deliberately_preserved: Create Draft, not Send Email — nothing is sent automatically.
The body wording, the `Hi <FirstName>,` opening and the `Dennis` sign-off, verbatim apart from the issuer-name fix.
Plain-text body, signature delimiter on, signature not rendered as HTML.
added_beyond_the_classic_zap: A `Reference: <PO number>` line in the body when the invoice has one. The classic Zap did not include it. It is here because an AP team matches a reminder against their PO, which is the whole point of the email — but it IS an addition to customer-facing copy, so it is called out here to be easy to remove: delete the `if (inv.reference)` push in buildBody.

known_gaps.one_reminder_per_invoice_only: This is the 1-day Zap, and the trigger delivers an invoice once as it crosses 1 day overdue. There is no 7-day or 30-day escalation. The classic Zap's name ('(1 Day)') implies siblings were intended; none were in the export. Adding one means another workflow with the same source and `days_overdue` changed — deploy it from this directory as a second entry in this file, the way luma-event-to-notion does.
known_gaps.repeat_drafts: No record is kept of invoices already drafted. A polling trigger re-delivering the same invoice would produce a second draft. Harmless — drafts do not send themselves, and a duplicate is visible in Drafts — so no Table was added.
known_gaps.no_overdue_invoices_at_migration_time: At 2026-07-28 Xero reported overdue_total 0.00 / overdue_count 0 (4 invoices awaiting payment, all due in August). So the happy path was verified by firing the workflow manually against INV-0077, a real but not-yet-overdue invoice, rather than by waiting for a genuine trigger delivery. The trigger itself is claimed and active; the first real delivery will be the earliest of the August invoices going a day past due.
